steps.heading: Clarify the problem
steps.body: Ask what the system must do, who will use it, and what is out of scope. Repeat the agreed requirements back to the interviewer.

steps.heading: List the main things
steps.body: Write down the important people and objects in the problem. Mark which ones need their own identity and which are just values, such as a time slot.

steps.heading: Give each class a job
steps.body: For every class, say what information it holds and what work it does. Note which behaviours may need different versions.

steps.heading: Show how the parts connect
steps.body: Draw the main classes and show which ones contain or use others. Include only the methods needed to explain the design.

steps.heading: Trace one complete task
steps.body: Follow the main use case from the first call to the final result. Add any missing class or method you discover.

steps.heading: Code the essential path
steps.body: Write the central classes and one working use case with clear names and type hints. Leave less important details for later.

steps.heading: Check failures and unusual cases
steps.body: Consider invalid input, two people acting at once, empty or full states, and cancellations. Decide how the code reports each problem.

steps.heading: Explain changes and choices
steps.body: Describe how you would add a feature and why you kept some possibilities out of the design.
